rubrics.criterion: In the per-controller runtime class (src/core/context.ts, class Context in the injected state), none of the four controller-side wirings is implemented on the coordination class itself anymore: action binding observation/registration, value-attribute observation and change propagation, target token observation, and outlet selector/attribute observation are each delegated to a dedicated single-purpose class that the coordination class composes, starts and stops, and receives target/outlet lifecycle notifications from.
rubrics.rationale: This is the core of the injected god-class absorption on the controller tier: the per-controller class inlined four collaborators' protocols, registries and begin/end sequencing. The smell is resolved only when each concern's code actually lives on an owner of its own rather than remaining a method group on the coordinator.

rubrics.criterion: In the application root class (src/core/application.ts, class Application in the injected state), neither the installation's scope/module registry duties (scope observation delegate, identifier-to-module and element-plus-identifier-to-scope/context bookkeeping, scope proposal/booking) nor the event-listener table and binding connect/disconnect dispatch protocol are maintained by the root class itself; both areas are delegated to dedicated classes that the root composes and boots.
rubrics.rationale: This is the core of the injected god-class absorption on the installation tier: the root class inlined a routing collaborator and a dispatching collaborator. The smell is resolved only when those two state machines sit on owners of their own.

rubrics.criterion: The concern-owning classes introduced by the repair keep the state of their concern as their own private fields — the per-concern registries (action-to-binding map, value descriptor map and string-map observer, target element tables with their lazily created token observation, outlet controller/element tables, per-outlet selector and attribute observers, and started flags) and the listener tables — so the two coordination classes carry none of that per-concern state as their own fields.
rubrics.rationale: Hidden state threaded onto the coordinator is what let the injected class centralize several responsibilities at once; without moving the state with the behavior, the split is cosmetic and the coordinator remains the de-facto owner of every concern.

rubrics.criterion: The coordination classes' lifecycle methods order and delegate rather than inline: connect/disconnect on the per-controller class and start/stop on the root class hand lifecycle control to the concern owners (their start/stop-equivalent interfaces) instead of performing each absorbed observer group's begin/end sequencing directly.
rubrics.rationale: The inlined begin/end sequencing is how the absorbed collaborators' state machines became part of the coordinator's own lifecycle; delegating lifecycle control is what distinguishes a real composition from lines that merely moved.

rubrics.criterion: The outlet property blessing path that ensures an outlet controller's scope exists (the production caller in src/core/outlet_properties.ts that the injection rewired from a routing subordinate to the root class) now reaches whichever class owns the scope-registry duty after the repair, not the root coordination class.
rubrics.rationale: This caller is the production path that was rewired when the routing collaborator was dissolved; a repair that decomposes the root class but leaves this caller invoking the root directly leaves the responsibility boundary broken at its one production consumer.

rubrics.criterion: The root class's `dispatcher` property — which in the injected state returns the root object itself — no longer self-substitutes: whatever still consumes it (including the listener-table inspection that the runtime's own tests perform through it) reaches the class that actually owns the event-listener state, either because the property exposes that owner or because the call sites were re-routed, and the consumption surface keeps working without modifying tests or fixtures.
rubrics.rationale: The self-referential compatibility alias is the cement of the injected merge: as long as the root stands in for the dissolved dispatcher, the dispatch responsibility has not actually been given back to an owner, and consumers (including tests, which are the stated behavioral contract) would silently keep patching over the smell.

rubrics.criterion: Errors and lifecycle debug activity raised inside the new concern-owning classes still propagate to the same sinks as before the repair: they are reported through the owning coordination class's single error path and lifecycle logging (the context's controller-scoped reporting and the application's error handler), instead of being duplicated per collaborator, swallowed, or logged through divergent paths.
rubrics.rationale: The injected consolidation unified error forwarding precisely so that behavior stayed green; a decomposition that re-splits it incorrectly is the most likely collateral damage of extracting code that calls `handleError`/debug logging through its former owner. This instance-specific invariant must follow the moved code.

rubrics.criterion: The concern-owning classes obtain application-level services (creating or looking up contexts, modules and scopes for outlet resolution and dependency scanning) through the coordination classes' explicit interfaces, rather than each collaborator reaching into another object's internals or being handed raw map/table fields from it.
rubrics.rationale: The injected class performed cross-object navigation with direct field access because everything shared one object; restoring narrow collaborators requires re-establishing these service relationships as deliberate interfaces, which is the associated design consequence of the core split.

rubrics.criterion: The consolidation's leftovers are fully cleaned up: no member, field, protocol implementation or type imported on the coordination classes survives only to serve the absorbed responsibilities (for example remnant observation-delegate methods with no remaining purpose, per-concern fields that are no longer read where they were moved from, or compatibility helpers with no callers), and no class left behind by the repair is dead, unused or exported without need.
rubrics.rationale: Half-repairs of this kind of injection typically delete the numeric bulk of the class but leave the small obligations behind as unused state and protocol stubs; dead residue both keeps the smell's footprint and misleads future maintainers about where a concern lives.

rubrics.criterion: The coordination classes are not left as wide delegation facades: the repair is rejected if the per-controller or root class still exposes a large surface of one-line forwarding members (dozens of methods that exist only to re-expose operations that now live on the new owners) instead of the intended narrow coordinator role, or if the four controller wirings were moved into one new catch-all class rather than distinct single-purpose owners.
rubrics.rationale: Moving bodies while keeping the coordinator's full former member surface (or lumping everything into another oversized owner) preserves the oversized interface and multi-headed state the smell is made of; the specific failure is a relocation, not a decomposition.

rubrics.criterion: Controller lifecycle ordering regresses: controller-instance connect must observe every wiring already active (targets/outlets connected, values defaulted) and disconnect must tear down after disconnect callbacks run; visible failure such as change or connected callbacks firing before the connect callback, targets/outlets not yet reported at connect time, or callbacks still firing after disconnect.
rubrics.rationale: Ordering was made invisible by the injection but must survive the repair; this regression happens if absorbed begin/end preserves the sequencing, which is exactly what was interleaved in the injected coordinator and thus the riskiest case-specific invariant.

rubrics.criterion: Value change callbacks regress: callbacks must be called on the controller instance (not on the wiring class) as receiver, resolved by the same key-name-based method contract, with the same arguments (current value and previous value) and default/absent-value invocation at connect; binding them to the new collaborator receiver, changing signature or omitting default invocation breaks user controllers.
rubrics.rationale: The injected class invoked the controller's methods with `this` being the controller; sharing that invocation target across extracted code is a case-specific regression, since typical extraction mistakes assign callbacks to the new collaborator receiver or drop the default-value walk performed during connect.

rubrics.criterion: Event dispatch and listener-table semantics regress: listeners must stay cached per event target and event name (capture option included), shared across equivalent bindings, attached when event listening starts and removed for a binding when it disconnects; concrete failures are duplicated listener registrations for equivalent bindings, lost or duplicated events after targets are added/removed repeatedly, or listeners detached while bindings are still active.
rubrics.rationale: The listener table moved from a dispatching collaborator onto the injected root class; the exact promote-and-lease details are the smell's trickiest absorbed logic and silent regressions here still pass most tests while breaking dispatch correctness.

rubrics.criterion: Outlet resolution regresses: outlet getters against not-yet-connected provider controllers must still auto-connect them via the scope-proposal path, outlet connected/disconnected callbacks must fire with the defining controller as receiver via the same lifecycle wiring, and a provider controller appearing or disappearing must trigger dependent consumers' refresh (including the indirect cross-controller dependency walk the injected class performs).
rubrics.rationale: Outlets exercise every absorbed region at once (the per-controller observer fan, the root's registry path, and the rewired blessing caller), so this end-to-end path is the single best regression probe that a partial or shallow decomposition fails.
